hero.lead: A nation of 35.1 million that completed its IMF programme in July 2026 after growth of 6 percent in 2025, and with a new $500 million road plan for its farms.

capital.heading: Ghana has rebuilt its credit, review by review. Next, a safe toilet in every home.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility, final review
register.note: Final disbursement of about $371 million; a 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument requested
register.text: Ghana completed every review, and asked the IMF to keep certifying its reforms without new lending.

register.name: Rural roads and market access
register.note: Feeder roads to farms and markets
register.text: Connects farming communities to the markets that pay for their harvests.

register.name: Secondary education and skills
register.text: Strengthens secondary education and the skills that lead to work.

register.name: Macroeconomic stability and resilient growth
register.text: Supports the reforms that steadied the economy and laid the ground for growth.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 59 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A lively street market in Accra, Ghana, colourful stalls

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Cocoa trees with ripening yellow pods on a smallholder farm in Ghana

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest canopy of Kakum National Park, Ghana

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: Lake Volta, Ghana, wide calm water with a wooden fishing canoe

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Akosombo hydropower dam on the Volta River, Ghana

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Ghana
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Ghana. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Ghanaians without a safely managed toilet at home: 81 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 43.5% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 35% cook with clean fuels and technology

guarantees.name: Education

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
